candidate_payload.research_markdown: The production boundary is finite: ten registered operational owners, 43 profiles, and five authority families. The stable gateway accepts only task_id, run_id, context_id, and intent_id and reconstructs the exact same-journal ActionIntent from the authenticated one-writer lifecycle. Preparation already contains normalized parameters, root bindings, and binding receipts; source locators must be reconstructed internally from its content-addressed artifact. The five families are LOCAL_STATE (13), GIT (6), DOCKER (10), CREDENTIAL (8), and OPERATOR (6), but some routes require a finite set of families rather than one owner-selected edge. Each route therefore needs a closed source_query_contract containing trusted locator reconstruction, read-only acquisition, typed raw result schema, terminal semantic predicate, receipt limitation, and explicit unavailable-authority state. Receipts prove effect ownership, while fresh domain reads prove semantic truth. Current acceptance captures cannot be promoted to production evidence. Missing provider implementations are future implementation work; their names, required inputs, fail-closed states, and verification boundary are finite and handed to planning.

exclusions: universal interception of ordinary Codex Bash, edit, browser, MCP, or subagent actions
global controller FD 198 or new Codex authentication/hook infrastructure
changing the 10 AVAILABLE / 6 CUSTODIAN_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED / 9 UNAVAILABLE classification
new owners, phase-ledger contracts, deployment, commit, push, secret access, external messages, or inferred acquisition paths
in_scope: the ten existing AVAILABLE owners and their 43 already-materialized profiles
an ID-only registered-owner execution gateway and work-memory one-writer production composition root
five production source-edge kinds: LOCAL_STATE, GIT, DOCKER, CREDENTIAL, and OPERATOR
existing source-owned receipts, owner sources, trusted-root contracts, provider handles, budget authority, and same-path tests in memory-knowledge and mcp-agents-workflow
charter.objective: Ground the finite production composition required to run the ten approved registered operational owners through PreventionController and OwnerRuntime, including an ID-only gateway, authoritative capacity and bindings, and real source-query contracts for the existing 43 owner/profile routes.
research_questions: How does the real registered-operation entrypoint reconstruct one already-recorded typed ActionIntent from task/run/context/intent identity without accepting owner argv, JSON, budgets, roots, or source edges?
What persisted one-writer ownership and repository-root evidence constructs the production PreventionJournal and controller composition root?
What exact trusted locator, acquisition method, result schema, and semantic predicate must each of the 43 existing profile routes materialize for the five source-edge kinds?

Which budget-capacity, binding-provider, approval, credential-handle, remote-repository, Docker, Git, local-state, and operator inputs already have authoritative acquisition routes, and which must fail closed?
What same-path evidence proves real execution, crash reconciliation, and semantic terminal verification without acceptance fixtures or universal Codex tool interception?
charter.supplied_input: The approved practical boundary governs registered operational workflows only. Audit proved the ten owners are acceptance-executable but lack a production controller composition, real source edges, external bindings, capacity construction, and materialized source acquisition recipes.
terminal_rules: PASS requires the core candidate, all three independent lenses, and adjudication to agree that every production acquisition route is grounded or explicitly fail closed.
GAPS means a correction remains possible from the two authoritative repositories.
BLOCKED means a required real provider, authority, or source locator has no accessible or named acquisition route.
No fixture-generated observation may be represented as production evidence.
